subject: Cross-border data paths & deployment preference — Finterra follow-up
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-08-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Cross-border data paths & deployment preference — Finterra follow-up

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Quick recap from this morning's discovery with Oliver (Finterra):

- Business context: Finterra is a European payments platform looking to add real-time fraud scoring and chat automation for merchant support across DE/FR/UK. They expect PII in prompts and want auditability for regulator reviews.
- Primary constraint: All customer-identifiable data must remain within the EU. No routing through US-based processing paths is acceptable.
- Preferred outcome: They are open to either Dedicated capacity (EU-only pools) or a Private VPC deployment inside their Azure tenancy. Hosted API is attractive for speed, but only if we can guarantee EU-only processing and separation — Oliver said their security team will not accept transient US hops.
- Timeline: PO talk within 8 weeks; pilot in 10–12 weeks if legal and infra alignment are good.
- Ask from Finterra: SOC2 evidence + a short matrix of hosting options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with clear notes on where data and metadata are stored and any cross-region fallbacks. They attached a questionnaire (will forward when received).

Open items for us:
1) Confirm whether our hosted EU region can be isolated end-to-end (no control-plane or telemetry routed via US).
2) If Hosted cannot satisfy, provide a rough-cost delta for Dedicated EU-only pools vs Private VPC onboarding (incl. KMS/HSM options).
3) Draft an answer for their SOC2 checklist (status + timeline for audit evidence).

Can Ben and Marissa pick this up and suggest a short (<10 slide) decision matrix we can share with Finterra's security team? I'll attach the call notes and record once I have permission.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — EMEA
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-20T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Cross-border data paths & deployment preference — Finterra follow-up

Nice summary, Jasmine. A few technical clarifications and proposals from my side: 

- Hosted API (EU region): Our hosted EU endpoints can keep inference compute within EU datacenters; however, the control plane and certain telemetry (billing, analytics) are currently aggregated in our US management plane. For strictly EU-only processing (no control-plane metadata leaving EU), we'd need to enable our "private-control-plane" option (available but requires ent. enablement and extra compliance review).
- Dedicated capacity: We can provision EU-only GPU pools with dedicated tenancy and tie KMS keys to EU KMS providers. This is the lower-effort option vs full Private VPC but still requires a reserved capacity commitment and lead time ~4–6 weeks for instance provisioning.
- Private VPC/on-prem: Full isolation, works for legal reqs; on-boarding includes network design, KMS integration, and an ops runbook. Timeline typically 8–12 weeks depending on customer's infra and approval cycles.

For the matrix, I'll draft a one-page table that highlights: data-at-rest location, control-plane footprint, telemetry/billing flow, KMS options, provisioning lead time, and estimated monthly starting cost range.

Action for Marissa: can you estimate the MRR starting point for a 4x A100 Dedicated pool vs ballpark engineering time/cost for Private VPC onboarding? If you want, I can sketch the infra diagram for both options.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@finterra.eu>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@finterra.eu
Date: 2027-08-21T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Cross-border data paths & deployment preference — Finterra follow-up

Thanks for the quick recap and the options. A few clarifications from Finterra security/legal: 

1) "EU-only processing" means both inference compute and any auxiliary caches/kv-store/prefix logs must not be exported outside the EU. Metadata (e.g., API keys usage) can be minimal but must be available for audits within EU logs if requested.
2) Control plane in the US is a blocker unless we have a contractual guarantee and technical proof that no customer data or customer-identifiable metadata leaves the EU.
3) KMS: we require customer-managed keys in an EU region (Azure Key Vault EU West or AWS KMS eu-west-1). HSM-backed keys preferred.
4) SOC2 evidence: please provide the SOC2 Type II report or your SOC2 attestor contact; we also included a short vendor questionnaire for you to fill.

Attached: Finterra_SOC2_Reqs.pdf (our standard vendor questionnaire) and a draft SOW template (finterra-sow-draft.xlsx).

We are leaning toward Dedicated EU pools as the fastest acceptable path, but if Redwood can offer Private VPC with a reasonable onboarding estimate, we'll evaluate total cost and time.

--
Oliver Schmidt
Head of Infrastructure
Finterra GmbH
